Distributing Node.js services with cluster

March 15, 2009 · 6 min read

Last week we shipped a small internal service that fans requests out to a pool of worker processes. A few people asked how we keep the workers honest, so here is the whole recipe: a supervisor, a heartbeat, and a boring amount of logging. The supervisor forks one worker per core and re-forks on exit; the heartbeat is a five-second ping over the IPC channel; and the logs go to syslog, because at 3am you do not want to be inventing log rotation.

The trick that surprised people is the graceful handoff. When a worker is told to retire, it stops accepting new connections but drains the ones it has, with a hard deadline of thirty seconds. The supervisor forks the replacement before sending the retirement notice, so capacity never dips. None of this is clever — it's just sequencing — but the sequencing is exactly the part everyone gets wrong the first time.

var cluster = require('cluster');
if (cluster.isMaster) {
  for (var i = 0; i < require('os').cpus().length; i++) cluster.fork();
} else {
  require('./service').listen(8080);
}

Next post: how we measure drain time in production without lying to ourselves about percentiles.
